newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FARMERS SAY BLOCKADE THREAT STILL STANDS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FARMERS SAY BLOCKADE THREAT STILL STANDS.

text.p: Hungarian farmers' union METESZ maintained its threat on Thursday to blockade border crossings after what it said was a government refusal of further talks.

"The government has squarely refused our Wednesday offer for negotiations," METESZ's leader Gyula Kosa told Reuters. "We do not expect any further development today and we will decide on Friday morning what the next step will be".

The union sent an ultimatum to the government on Monday threatening to block border crossings and roads to Budapest unless a demand for unconditional tax relief for farmers earning less than 1.5 million forints ($8,500) a year is met.
Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze warned the farmers on Wednesday that police would prevent METESZ, which is one of several farmers unions, from carrying out its threat.

Jozsef Veress, deputy cabinet chief of Prime Minister Gyula Horn, sent a letter to METESZ on Wednesday inviting its leaders to take part in a nationwide debate about a newly devised 10-year farming policy draft.
The letter said most of METESZ's claims are connected to the farming policy draft and the government is prepared to discuss all the issues within the framework of the nationwide debate.
Horn has ceded to farmers' union demands for roundtable talks to solve the crisis that has hit Hungarian agriculture. He announced on Tuesday that the talks would take place on April 25 to 27.

Veress's letter also said the government has already yielded to 10 of an original set of 14 demands from METESZ and that the union has failed to show up at two tentative meetings with government officials.

A February demonstration in the central Hungarian town of Kiskoros sparked a series of farmers' protests following the government's 1997 income and social security tax increases for individual farmers.
Hungary has almost 30 farmers' unions which sometimes have conflicting interests regarding land ownership, taxation and subsidy issues.
